modelingNotes: Exact order 3036356, gray; a catalog candidate selected from a representative industrial materials list, not confirmation of its purchase or installed strip position.

A1/A2/B1/B2 are neutral authoring identifiers for ordinary wire clamps, not manufacturer-printed numbers or the project terminal-strip position. A is the left side of the cited circuit diagram; B is the right side. Unused keys do not exist on smaller variants.

A1 and A2 are the permanently common twin side. B1 is across the knife. The knife is drawn open in the manufacturer diagram; normal_state=open records that reference depiction, not a measured operating state. Never author a permanent jumper from A to B to represent the switch.

Only authored wires, jumpers and terminated cable cores join physical nets. Function symbols never create continuity. Shared connection policy accommodates the internal-common representation; it does not authorize arbitrary multiple external conductors in one clamp.
Ordinary passive clamps are not universally required. Projects may require selected external connections using connectionReview; unused clamp capacity is legitimate.

The IEC nominal capability is attached to each ordinary point for inspection, not multiplied by the number of clamps. Ratings are subject to the catalog conductor, bridge, installation and approval conditions; the compiler does not verify these conditions or aggregate block current.

The ordinary block has no protective-earth, shield or power-supply terminal. DIN-rail mounting does not make this a PE terminal. Optional bridge shafts, test interfaces and fitted accessories are not modeled.

IEC catalog rating: 400 V, 20 A; maximum 20 A with 4 mm2 conductor subject to total connected-conductor current. Solid 0.08-4 mm2; stranded 0.08-2.5 mm2; ferruled 0.14-2.5 mm2; stripping 10 mm. Bridge accessories have their own ratings.

connectionCoverage.notes: All 3 ordinary spring-cage wire clamps are inventoried. Accessory bridge/test interfaces and accessory assemblies are unmodeled. Fixed internal commoning requires explicit project jumpers; switch state and clamp occupancy limits are not evaluated.
